intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor — front-line via RASolute 303 (NCT07491445)
expected_benefit: OS HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53, p=4.6e-11) in the 2L RAS G12 population including KRAS G12D; median OS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo, mPFS 7.2 vs 3.6 mo, ORR 31.6% (RASolute 302, n=500). First-line benefit is inferred and rests on the unread RASolute 303.
key_risks: mucocutaneous toxicity drives dose reductions in an older patient even with a management algorithm
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: YES (RASolute 303 recruiting front-line, accepts KRAS G12D under the RAS-mutant criterion); oral modality (no stated constraint, but relevant at 79); efficacy/toxicity weight 0.5 neutral — free_text warns age 79 may justify a more toxicity-averse setting, which is the one soft spot here.
guideline_status: No NCCN category yet (NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 lists no KRAS G12D agent). Only feature-targeting agent with a positive randomized phase 3 plus FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation; NCCN names clinical-trial participation as the preferred route for an actionable finding.
rationale_summary: Four of five personas placed this at rank 1 and all five endorsed it; it is the one feature-targeting option carrying randomized phase 3 evidence. The conservative, critic, and concensusite rank it first on evidence depth and proximity-to-guideline, not on a settled first-line benefit. The registration data sit at 2L while this man is treatment-naive, so the front-line claim rests on the unread RASolute 303, and his G12D estimate is borrowed from the RAS G12 stratum rather than a per-allele analysis. The risktaker and advocate dissented on patient-facing tolerability: both noted the neutral 0.5 weight understates a 79-year-old's likely toxicity aversion, and prefers_trials does not separate this from the gentler allele-matched zoldonrasib since both recruit front-line. The pan-RAS mechanism covers any subclonal RAS escape the ctDNA has not yet shown. No veto.
open_questions: RASolute 303 first-line OS and safety in a treatment-naive 79-year-old have not read out
G12D-specific benefit is inferred from the RAS G12 subgroup, not a pre-specified per-allele analysis
tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA G12D call strengthens trial eligibility (workup, not a gate to candidacy)
likelihood_of_effect: High in 2L RAS G12 PDAC — OS HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53) in RASolute 302 (n=500); first-line benefit inferred from the unread RASolute 303.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (rash G3+ 14%, stomatitis G3+ 12%; G3+ TRAE 43.6% overall, below chemo)

counter_productive_moa.description: Mucocutaneous toxicity can force dose reductions that erode the exposure the survival signal depends on; no mechanism-level antagonism of the therapeutic goal.

overall: The only feature-targeting option with randomized phase 3 survival evidence; first-line benefit inferred from an unread trial and the allele estimate borrowed from a RAS G12 subgroup.

intervention_label: zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), KRAS G12D(ON)-selective inhibitor — front-line via RASolute 305 (NCT07621718)
expected_benefit: ORR 30% with 80% disease control in KRAS G12D PDAC at his exact allele (phase 1, n=40); no 95% CI on ORR and PFS/DoR not yet reported. Front-line RASolute 305 adds it to the chemotherapy backbone.
key_risks: low-grade GI: nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%, vomiting 15%, rash 10% — almost all grade 1-2
no grade 4 or 5 treatment-related events at 1200 mg/day
additive myelosuppression with the RASolute 305 chemo backbone is unquantified (no published combination-toxicity table)
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: YES (RASolute 305 recruiting, requires KRAS G12D); gentlest agent in the dossier, which the free_text's age-79 note argues for past the literal 0.5 weight; advocate would lead with this for an older patient.
guideline_status: No NCCN category (NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 lists no KRAS G12D agent). NCCN names trial enrollment as the preferred route for an actionable finding; RASolute 305 is a randomized double-blind front-line phase 3 at the patient's exact allele.
rationale_summary: All five personas endorsed this and it matches the patient's exact G12D allele with the cleanest toxicity in the dossier — no grade 4/5 events, rash only 10%. The advocate and risktaker would lead with it for a 79-year-old, since the free_text flags that the neutral 0.5 weight understates likely toxicity aversion. The critic and concensusite dissented on ranking it at the top: it is an n=40 single-arm phase 1 abstract with no CI on the 30% ORR and no mature PFS/DoR, so durability is unmeasured and a response rate without a time-to-event anchor is the surrogate the critic discounts. Those dissents are about rank position over the randomized daraxonrasib evidence, not about using the drug; both concede the allele match is real and RASolute 305 is the guideline-preferred route in. The chemo-combination toxicity in RASolute 305 has not been reported on its own. No veto.
open_questions: mature PFS/DoR and a 95% CI on the 30% ORR are not in the ASCO GI abstract
RASolute 305 has no published dedicated combination-toxicity table, so additive myelosuppression at 79 is unquantified
whether the G12D-selective agent reproduces the preclinical FAS/CD8 immune-reprogramming seen with the tool compound MRTX1133 at clinical exposures is untested
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate, allele-matched — ORR 30% / DCR 80% in G12D PDAC (phase 1, n=40, no CI; PFS/DoR immature). RASolute 305 will test it front-line.
toxicity_burden: Low (nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%, rash 10%; no G4/5 events at monotherapy dose)

counter_productive_moa.description: Critic and concensusite dissented on the thin single-arm evidence base; durability unmeasured, so on-target activity may not translate to a durable effect.

overall: The allele-matched, gentlest agent in the set — best tolerability for a 79-year-old, but the evidence is a single-arm n=40 abstract with no durability readout.

intervention_label: INCB161734, KRAS G12D-selective inhibitor — front-line + chemo via DAWN-303 (NCT07522073)
expected_benefit: ORR 37% with 78% disease control in heavily pretreated KRAS G12D PDAC (phase 1, n=41), the strongest single-agent response in the dossier; mPFS/mDoR not reached at ~5 mo follow-up. DAWN-303 tests it front-line on a chemo backbone.
key_risks: grade >=3 neutropenia ~40% in the chemo-combination cohort the patient would actually enter
monotherapy GI toxicity 50-60% but grade 1-2, with rash and stomatitis notably absent
no treatment-related deaths; no dedicated combination-safety characterization
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: YES (DAWN-303 recruiting, requires KRAS G12D, enrolls previously untreated PDAC; phase 1 parent NCT06179160 also takes him front-line); the front-line construct bundles chemotherapy, and the ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia works against a 79-year-old the neutral 0.5 weight does not protect.
guideline_status: No NCCN category (NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 lists no KRAS G12D agent). A second sponsor's G12D-selective agent; enrollable only through DAWN-303, not as standard care.
rationale_summary: All five personas endorsed this and it carries the strongest single-agent response number on the board, 37% ORR with 78% DCR, with monotherapy toxicity that stays grade 1-2 and spares rash and stomatitis. The critic and concensusite read the 37% vs 30% gap against zoldonrasib as within-noise across two tiny uncontrolled cohorts, so it sits at the same evidence level rather than above the allele-matched agent. The conservative dissented specifically on the construct the patient would actually enter: DAWN-303 stacks the inhibitor on mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab-paclitaxel, and the phase 1 combination cohort already showed ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia — synergistic marrow toxicity with no dedicated combination-safety trial, the pattern the conservative flags at 79. The favorable monotherapy profile is real, but the enrollable front-line arm carries an uncharacterized marrow burden. No veto.
open_questions: the 37% ORR comes from a single-sponsor phase 1 abstract (n=41) with immature PFS/DoR
grade >=3 neutropenia ~40% in the chemo combination is not characterized in a dedicated combination-safety trial
first-line durability is unproven; the response signal is from heavily pretreated patients
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate to high single-agent — ORR 37% / DCR 78% in pretreated G12D PDAC (phase 1, n=41, no CI; PFS not reached at ~5 mo). DAWN-303 tests it front-line.
toxicity_burden: High (combination-cohort G3+ neutropenia ~40%; monotherapy GI 50-60% grade 1-2)

counter_productive_moa.description: Conservative dissented on additive marrow toxicity: chemo-combination neutropenia can force dose reductions in an older patient that erode delivered intensity.

overall: Strongest single-agent response number in the dossier, but the enrollable front-line construct bundles chemotherapy with ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia and no dedicated combination-safety data.

intervention_label: ceralasertib (AZD6738), ATR inhibitor (ARID1A synthetic-lethal axis) — via NCT03682289, gated on BAF250a IHC loss
expected_benefit: Confirmed ORR 14% (4/29) across all ARID1A-deficient tumors; the 31% figure is a gynecologic-histology subset (endometrioid endometrial, ovarian clear cell) with no pancreatic responder shown. mDoR 33.7 mo in gynecologic responders.
key_risks: ATR-class cytopenias (anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia) — per-term grade >=3 rates not broken out in the abstract; only the zero treatment-related-death count is reported
class anemia is the dose-limiting effect for ATR inhibitors (grade 3 anemia ~26-36% in related agents) and is limiting in an older patient
entry requires BAF250a IHC loss; only ~67% (28/42) of ARID1A-mutant tumors lose the protein, so the frameshift call alone does not confirm eligibility
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: PARTIAL (NCT03682289 takes pancreatic tumors stratified by ARID1A status, but it is active-not-recruiting, so the open trial a trials-leaning patient wants is not currently available); oral modality.
guideline_status: No NCCN category; no society names ATR inhibition for PDAC. Reading a gynecologic subset across to basal-like PDAC is off-indication extrapolation that no guideline endorses for this histology. Kept as a trial-only banked second axis.
rationale_summary: Every persona ranked this last and the synthesis formula's 1.0 score is an artifact of the board spending its round-2 critiques on the top-tier disagreement, not a signal that ceralasertib outranks the KRAS agents — the unanimous round-1 order puts it below all three RAS-directed options. It is the weakest evidence on the board for this patient: confirmed ORR 14% across all ARID1A-deficient tumors with the activity concentrated in gynecologic histologies and no PDAC responder shown, so the pancreatic rationale is cross-tumor extrapolation backed by colorectal/ovarian preclinical work with no PDAC line tested. Entry is gated on BAF250a IHC loss the frameshift does not establish, so it is not even confirmed enrollable, and per-term ATR-class cytopenias are unquantified in a 79-year-old. The personas keep it on the list as a mechanistically independent banked axis if the KRAS routes fail, not as a present recommendation. The EZH2 arm of this axis lost its lead agent when tazemetostat was withdrawn, leaving ATR as the live route. No dissent or veto was lodged in round 2, but no persona endorsed it above rank 4.
open_questions: no pancreatic responder in the clinical ARID1A data; PDAC relevance is inferred
per-term grade >=3 cytopenia rates are not reported in the abstract
BAF250a IHC loss is required and the ctDNA/tissue frameshift call alone does not confirm it
the lead ARID1A basket is active-not-recruiting, so the enrollable door is not currently open
likelihood_of_effect: Low for PDAC — confirmed ORR 14% across ARID1A-deficient tumors (pmid:41686845), activity concentrated in gynecologic histologies with zero pancreatic responders shown.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (ATR-class anemia / thrombocytopenia / neutropenia; per-term G3+ rates unreported, zero treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: Cross-tumor extrapolation with no PDAC responder; the synthetic-lethal effect may not engage in basal-like PDAC, and class anemia limits exposure at 79.

overall: A mechanistically independent banked second axis off the ARID1A frameshift, but no PDAC responder exists, entry is BAF250a-IHC-gated, and the lead basket is not recruiting.
